title: Sport science teacher
description: Company Description High school is an educational institution dedicated to providing inclusive, quality secondary education to learners from diverse backgrounds. The school focuses on strong academic foundations, personal development, and preparation for higher education and future careers. It promotes a supportive environment where students can grow intellectually, socially, and physically. title: Development of a vector control training package for wash and health practitioners in the africa region.
description:

Introduction The Netherlands Red Cross (NLRC) and partners are working to strengthen local capacities for emergency preparedness, anticipatory action, and response across Africa. In line with their auxiliary role to the public authorities, and within the framework of localization, National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies frequently act as first responders during disease outbreaks, flooding, displacement crises, and other emergencies. Vector-borne diseases continue to pose a significant public health burden in many countries where the Red Cross and Red Crescent National Societies operate. At the same time, vector control knowledge among WASH and Health practitioners varies considerably. There is a need for accessible, practical training materials that can be used by National Societies, surge personnel, and humanitarian practitioners to improve knowledge and decision-making related to vector control. The NLRC therefore seeks a consultant to develop a comprehensive training package on vector control that can be delivered by facilitators with a fair understanding of the subject matter. The package will be piloted during a training event planned for December 2026 in either Ethiopia or South Sudan. 2. Background and Context Vector-borne diseases remain among the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in many humanitarian settings. Climate change, population movements, urbanization, environmental degradation, and weak health systems are contributing to changes in disease transmission patterns and increasing the risk of outbreaks. Humanitarian organizations are increasingly expected to integrate vector control considerations into emergency preparedness, response, recovery, and resilience programmes. While specialist expertise is sometimes available, many WASH and Health practitioners involved in programme design and implementation have limited formal training in vector control. The Red Cross movement has an important role to play through: Community engagement , risk communication and behaviour change Environmental management Vector surveillance and risk assessment Support to outbreak preparedness and response including community-based surveillance Coordination with health and WASH actors Integration of vector control into humanitarian programming To strengthen these capacities, a practical training package is required that can be delivered in different country contexts and adapted to local disease priorities. 3. Purpose, Objectives and Deliverables Purpose To develop a practical, participatory and easy-to-facilitate vector control training package for WASH and Health practitioners working in humanitarian and development settings. Overall Objective To increase the knowledge and understanding of vector-borne disease prevention and vector control among WASH and Health practitioners, enabling them to support the design, implementation and monitoring of appropriate vector control interventions. Specific Objectives The training package should enable participants to: Understand the epidemiology and transmission pathways of major vector-borne diseases. Understand the roles and responsibilities of WASH, Health and community actors in vector control. Conduct basic vector-related risk assessments. Select appropriate vector control interventions based on context and risk. Understand operational, environmental and safety considerations. Integrate vector control into preparedness, anticipatory action and humanitarian emergency responses. Coordinate with relevant health, WASH and government stakeholders. Scope of the Training Package The consultant should develop a 3 days training package with different modules and exercises, allowing for a one to three days training depending on the modules used. The training should cover, at minimum: Vector-borne Diseases Introduction to: Malaria (with description of different malaria carrying subspecies) Dengue, Chikungunya, Yellow Fever, Schistosomiasis, Trypanosomiasis and other relevant diseases common in African humanitarian settings Vector Control Approaches Introduction to Environmental mechanical biological and chemical and integrated Vector Management (IVM). Humanitarian Context The context considered for the training include, vector control during emergencies**,** vector control during displacement and camp settings, Flood-related vector risks, Urban vector control challenges as well as for the Red Cross important Community-based approaches, and Protection, Gender and Inclusion (PGI) Planning and Decision Making The training should include a section focusing on health and surveillance data, risk assessment, Intervention selection, Monitoring and evaluation, Coordination mechanisms Safety and Environmental Considerations This should include Safe handling of equipment and chemicals Environmental risks Waste management Safeguarding and community acceptance Emerging and other relevant Topics Climate change and vector-borne diseases Insecticide resistance, new and emerging vector control tools such as spatial repellents, Operational challenges in humanitarian settings Deliverables The consultant will with the support of the NLRC and UNICEF will be expected to provide: Review and compilation of existing vector control training materials from organizations such as: IFRC, WHO, UNICEF and NGO’s working on vector control and identify materials that can be adapted and referenced. The consultant will develop a complete facilitator package in English including: Facilitator guide, Agenda for a 3-day version, Session plans, Facilitation notes, Interactive exercises Possible case studies and group work exercises, Quizzes and knowledge checks Participant package that should include: Participant manual, Handouts, Reference materials, Reading list Links to online resources PowerPoint presentation deck(s) suitable for use by non-specialist facilitators. Training evaluation package including: Pre-training assessment Post-training assessment Participant evaluation forms Facilitation of a pilot training in December 2026 in Ethiopia South Sudan or other country in the region and incorporation of lessons learned into the final training package(optional). 4. Profile of the Desired Consultant The consultant should possess: Minimum 7 years of professional experience in vector control, public health, entomology, or related fields. Demonstrated experience in humanitarian settings. Experience with vector control in Africa, preferably in both emergency and development contexts. Proven experience in developing training curricula and adult learning materials. Strong facilitation skills. Experience working with Red Cross/Red Crescent, UN agencies, government institutions or international NGOs is an advantage. Excellent written and spoken English. Experience integrating participatory adult learning methodologies. 5. Methodology The consultant is expected to: Conduct a brief desk review of existing training resources. Consult with NLRC, IFRC, UNICEF and selected technical experts. Develop draft training materials. Revise materials based on feedback. Facilitate the pilot training. Produce a final training package reflecting lessons learned from the pilot. 6. Planning Indicative timeline: Activity Timeline Contracting consultant - Week of 9th November 2026 Desk review and consultations - November 20th 2026 Draft training package - November 25th 2026 Review and revisions - December 5th 2026 Pilot training (optional time permitting) - December 2026 Final training package - December 2026 7. Climate and Environmental Impact The consultant should ensure that: The training promotes environmentally responsible vector control approaches. Environmental and ecological risks of vector control interventions are adequately addressed. Preference is given to sustainable and integrated vector management approaches. Training delivery methods minimize environmental impact where feasible. 8. Responsibilities and Communication The assignment will be coordinated by: Jan Heeger, WASH Programme Advisor, NLRC Selam Seje, Health Advisor, NLRC Joey de Hamer, Programme Manager, NLRC Peter Mamburi IFRC technical focal points Submission Deadline The proposal shall be submitted before the deadline for reception of applications on the 4th of October 2026. title: HEAD OF OFFICE (M/F/D), ETHIOPIA
description:
The German Red Cross (GRC) assists people affected by disasters, crises and armed conflicts, and is a committed advocate for the fundamental principles of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement. Our Mission: We provide needs-based, flexible, innovative and sustainable support to Sister National Societies, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC), and the wider humanitarian community. We enable early and immediate life-saving assistance and implement anticipatory action and risk-reducing activities, particularly in the face of climate change and armed conflicts and their humanitarian consequences. As a partner, facilitator and convener of cooperation, we strive to fulfil commitments to localization, community participation, protection and inclusion, gender and diversity, accountability, and learning. Through these efforts, we aim to build resilient communities and ensure effective and inclusive humanitarian responses in an increasingly complex global landscape. The GRC is currently seeking an experienced Head of Office (m/f/d) to lead its Country Office in Ethiopia. The GRC has a long-standing partnership with the Ethiopian Red Crescent Society (ERCS). At present, the primary focus of GRC lies in providing assistance to the ERCS in addressing the ongoing crisis and humanitarian needs and adjusting the existing portfolio according to the changing needs and according to ERCS priorities The GRC is committed to support its Sister Society where possible and work with the ERCS team to jointly decide on long-term programmes which fall within ERCS strategic priorities through joint programs, exchange of knowledge as well as technical and managerial support. The Head of Office (HoO) is located in Addis Abeba. He/she directly supervises the international GRC delegates and national staff and is responsible for the overall security management. The HoO reports to the country manager at GRC HQ in Berlin. title: Regional Safety & Security Director
description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. Context The East Africa region supports effective, efficient, and high-quality programming by strengthening capacity around client outcomes, program quality, strategic positioning, and business development. It addresses overlapping humanitarian and development challenges – conflict, weak governance, and environmental degradation – through integrated, impactful approaches. The region prioritizes cross-learning, innovation, and harmonized technical strategies, especially in high-need areas. It ensures continuity of care and coordinated service delivery for clients on the move, while advancing strategic donor engagement through cohesive fundraising and regional collaboration. The region responds swiftly to country program needs, filling critical gaps and navigating access constraints, emergencies, and security shifts. It amplifies client and frontline voices to inform global advocacy and fosters strong team cohesion to enhance program delivery. EA focuses on cost-efficient and adaptive approaches to the evolving humanitarian and donor landscape, with a clear focus on resourcing country programs. The EA region operates country programs in Uganda, Kenya, Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, and Ethiopia. Position Summary The Regional Safety and Security Director (RSSD) is one of the most senior leadership roles in the East Africa region and provides strategic leadership for safety, security, and humanitarian access across the region. They set and drive the implementation of a comprehensive strategy to anticipate, analyze, and mitigate risks, safeguard staff and assets, enable principled humanitarian access, and ensure the continuity of IRC’s operations and programs in complex and high-risk environments. As the principal safety and security advisor to, and close partner of, the Regional Vice President (RVP), the RSSD works alongside the RVP on the decisions that shape IRC’s presence, access, and continuity across the region. They are a full member of the Regional Management Team and of IRC’s global safety and security (S&S) team. Within the Regional Management Team, the RSSD contributes as a senior leader to regional strategy, priorities, and decision-making, not only as the safety and security function, bringing a risk-informed perspective to program, operational, and resourcing choices. They integrate Gender, Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (GEDI) informed security risk analysis into strategic, operational, programmatic, and partnership decisions so that security considerations are embedded across IRC’s work. Reporting jointly to the RVP and the Senior Director for Safety and Security (SDSS), the RSSD operates with significant autonomy and influence. Working in close partnership with Country Directors, they ensure that each country program has robust, context-appropriate protocols, systems, and capacities in place to address unique threats and challenges, while remaining agile to adapt to shifting environments. The RSSD maintains in-depth knowledge of security dynamics across all EA countries, monitors early warning indicators, and deploys regularly, including at short notice, to support local teams. They play a central role in mentoring and building the capabilities of IRC staff and leaders to operate safely and effectively, thereby strengthening IRC’s ability to reach and serve the most affected and underserved populations. Responsibilities Strategic Leadership and Regional Management As a member of the Regional Management Team, contribute as a senior leader to regional strategy, priority-setting, and decision-making, bringing a risk-informed perspective to program, operational, and resourcing choices across the region rather than representing the safety and security function alone. Serve as the principal safety and security advisor to, and close partner of, the RVP, enabling timely, risk-informed decisions on humanitarian access, operational continuity, and duty of care, and jointly activating and leading crisis management when required. Partner with Country Directors to align safety, security, and humanitarian access with country Strategy Action Plans (SAPs) and operational priorities, supporting their decision-making and accountability for risk. Security Risk Management Lead and supervise the identification, analysis, and mitigation of S&S risks across the region, ensuring alignment with IRC’s global standards. Guide and support Country Directors and field leaders to adapt and implement context-specific security risk management strategies ensuring proactive risk identification, mitigation, and emergency preparedness. Review, monitor, and encourage compliance with the Security Minimum Standards (SMS) in all country programs providing follow-up and technical guidance where gaps are identified. Drive and champion the development, adaptation, and roll-out of global and regional initiatives on duty of care and safeguarding, embedding these into operational culture and practice. Shape and strengthen safety and security policies, procedures, and practices that fully integrate Gender Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion (GEDI) principles as well as Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results System (PEERS) commitments. Extend IRC’s security capacity to partners, ensuring they receive tailored risk management support, access to systems, and benefit from IRC’s standards relevant to their operational contexts. Build and maintain an active network of IRC security focal points across country programs and cultivate strong external relationships with professional contacts, peer agencies, and security counterparts to enhance collective risk management. Humanitarian Access Management Enable and safeguard principled, secure, and sustained humanitarian access across country programs, ensuring communities can be reached and served in line with IRC’s country Strategy Action Plans (SAP). Strengthen and expand humanitarian access teams and capabilities across the region, building skills, systems, and approaches that enhance operational reach and acceptance. Develop, adapt, and implement context-specific guidelines for humanitarian access and engagement with state and non-state actors, ensuring alignment with IRC policy, international humanitarian law, and standards. Advise and guide country programs in the design of operational and programmatic contingency plans ensuring preparedness for sudden shifts in political, security, or conflict dynamics. Collaborate with relevant IRC units to ensure prompt and appropriate follow-up to violations of IRC’s Code of Conduct and breaches of humanitarian principles, reinforcing accountability and ethical operations. Performance Management and Development Lead and actively contribute to the recruitment and selection of key positions with S&S responsibilities, ensuring high-caliber talent and diverse representation. Co-manage and mentor direct-report staff (under the Management in Partnership (MiP) model with Country Directors), setting clear expectations, defining performance objectives, providing regular, timely feedback, and conducting documented performance reviews that drive accountability and growth. Promote and safeguard staff well-being, monitoring staff care across the region and supporting appropriate interventions to address the needs of both national and international staff. Directly supervise and develop the Regional Humanitarian Access and Safety Coordinator, ensuring progressive and forward-looking S&S plans that align with regional priorities and organizational strategy. Learning & Development Design, support, and supervise the implementation of regional capacity-building plans, ensuring effective delivery of IRC’s global S&S training programs across EA country programs. Embed gender-sensitive approaches into all capacity development and learning initiatives, addressing gender-specific risks and ensuring inclusivity in staff preparedness. Lead and facilitate critical incident management trainings and simulations, in close coordination with the global S&S unit to strengthen preparedness and response capacities across the region. Incident Management Support country programs to ensure timely, accurate, and high-quality incident notification, reporting, analysis, and dissemination of lessons learned. Serve as a member of the Regional Incident Management Team actively supporting the RVP in the management and resolution of Tier 2 and Tier 3 incidents. Facilitate After-Action Reviews ensuring that corrective measures are clearly defined, documented, and systematically implemented in line with established incident protocols. Oversee and monitor the SHIELD incident database producing quarterly trend analyses to inform strategic decision-making and strengthen regional risk mitigation. Key Working Relationships Reports to: Regional Vice President, East Africa, and Senior Director, Global Safety & Security (matrixed reporting) Member of: Regional Management Team and IRC’s global Safety & Security team Partners closely with: the Regional Vice President, as principal safety and security advisor, and Country Directors on country risk, humanitarian access, and duty of care Manages: Regional Humanitarian Access & Security Coordinator; and, through Management in Partnership with the respective Country Directors, country Security Leads Collaborates with: fellow Regional Safety & Security Directors, the Director of Security Learning & Operations, the Global Duty of Care Director, People & Culture, and other members of the Regional Management Team; and, externally, with peer agencies, security networks, and relevant counterparts Qualifications & Requirements At least 10 years’ experience in international humanitarian assistance, with proven ability to plan, organize, and lead security management operations. Prior experience in EA with strong knowledge of regional and country dynamics is essential. Fluency in English required; proficiency in a relevant regional language (e.g. Arabic, Amharic, Somali, or Swahili) is an asset. Demonstrated grounding in humanitarian principles, codes of conduct, NGO culture, and proven success in gender-sensitive security management and gender equality. Skilled at influencing without authority and building effective relationships across multinational teams, partners, and stakeholders. Demonstrated ability to transfer knowledge through mentoring, coaching, and non-formal methods. Strong capacity to analyze and present complex security dynamics and incidents clearly and on short notice, highlighting implications for operations. Willingness and ability to travel up to 40% of the time. Work Environment This position is open to both national and international applicants, in the locations indicated as well as potentially other IRC locations open to hosting. We will, however, prioritize consideration of national candidates from the region and for which our highly competitive national salary scale and benefits will apply. Returning National Candidates: We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the Country in which this position is based, are currently located outside your home country, and possess over 4 years of international work experience, the IRC has introduced an attractive remuneration package. The package includes competitive compensation, return flight to post, shipping allowance, temporary housing, and a relocation allowance. Certain restrictions may apply. IRC strives to attract, motivate, and retain qualified national staff in our programs. Gender Equality, Diversity and Inclusion: at IRC, we are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity. Organizations that are diverse in age, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, nationality, and perspective are validated to be better organizations. More importantly, creating a safe workspace environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best is the right thing to do. So, bring your whole self to work. We particularly encourage qualified women to apply for this role, and are committed to supporting them through flexible working arrangements, safety and duty of care planning tailored to the East African countries’ context, and a workplace culture that values the leadership women bring to humanitarian response. In keeping with our core values of Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality, IRC strives to maintain a work environment built on mutual respect in which all individuals treat each other professionally, and free of bias, prejudice, and harassment. IRC expressly prohibits and will not tolerate discrimination, harassment, retaliation, or bullying of IRC Persons in any work setting. All IRC staff, wherever they are located, are accountable for creating an environment free of discrimination, harassment, bullying, and retaliation. Professional Standards: All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct . Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding , Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Pre-Hospital Emergency Care (PHEC) Delegate Ethiopia (m/f/d)

Uganda: Wakiso and Kampala districts. Ethiopia: Addis Ababa and Hawassa. South Africa: City of Johannesburg, Ekurhuleni and Tshwane. Nigeria: Abuja FCT and Nasarawa. Burkina Faso: Ouagadougou and Bobo-Dioulasso. Firms can apply for one or more markets where they can demonstrate the ability to deliver the assignments. Firms must be registered in each country where they seek to provide the services. Objective of the audit The primary objective is to verify that sub-grantees are operating in full compliance with the financial, risk management, and statutory requirements of their signed grant agreements and relevant regulatory standards. The audit will assess: Financial accountability, internal controls, and complete expenditure documentation. Compliance with anti-fraud, anti-corruption, and financial risk governance mandates. Accuracy, integrity, and reconciliation of financial and transactional data across reporting frameworks. Adherence to statutory obligations, procurement guidelines, and budget line allocations. Scope of audit Expenditure verification: Reconcile transaction listings, general ledgers, and bank statements against approved budget lines and the project scope of work. Milestone achievement: Verify that disbursements are linked to confirmed deliverables as per the signed agreements. Expenditure verification and anti-double dipping: Verify that all incurred expenditures are legitimate, supported by adequate documentation, and that there is no “double dipping” or duplicate funding from other sources for the same activities. External audit review: Review external audit management reports and prior audit findings for the last two financial years. Test to ensure that all recommendations arising from findings have been implemented. Procurement compliance: Inspect procurement documentation to ensure competitive bidding policies were followed. Internal controls: Evaluate sub-recipient internal controls, including segregation of duties, delegation of authority, and financial software controls. Conduct walkthroughs for various cycles, including payments, payroll and assets, ensuring they are in line with policy. Statutory compliance: Confirm compliance with statutory obligations, including tax filings, labour laws, and anti-corruption policies. Deliverables Audit plan: Detailed timeline and 100% review for selected sub-grantees. Individual audit reports: Comprehensive audit reports for each sub-grantee featuring granular findings, objective risk ratings (Compliant / Partially Compliant / Non-Compliant), root-cause analysis of compliance gaps, and actionable, time-bound Corrective Action Plans (CAPs) complete with clear implementation deadlines, designated responsible owners, and re-verification milestones to ensure full risk mitigation. Summary consolidation: High-level overview of systemic compliance gaps and recommended training/capacity-building interventions. Qualifications of firms and proposed personnel The selected firm and its proposed personnel must demonstrate a comprehensive profile aligned with financial audit and risk compliance requirements. Mandatory qualifications include: Extensive experience in conducting financial, forensic, and risk compliance audits within the NGO and development sectors. Proven technical expertise in financial risk management, internal controls assessment, and fraud prevention/detection methodologies. Certified financial and risk audit professionals, such as CPA, ACCA, CFE, or equivalent certifications. Strong analytical skills in financial data reconciliation, transaction testing, and identifying systemic governance and control gaps. Experience in reviewing grant agreements, evaluating statutory compliance, and producing actionable financial audit reports. Evaluation criteria Proposals should: Be clear about the relevant skills, experience and capacity of the participant in respect of this particular scope of work. Contain details of the proposed approach to be adopted to deliver the service in accordance with the scope of work. Clearly indicate whether bid participants have the capacity to meet the requirements of the scope of work. Clearly indicate compliance with the appropriate data protection, privacy, legal, social, tax and ethical requirements applicable to each country applied for. Bidders must be registered firms in the countries where they seek to provide the services. A firm can bid for one or more markets depending on capacity. Proposals will be evaluated against the following criteria: 1. Experience, skills and ability of the service provider — 30% Past experience in similar work of this nature. Team member experience, accompanied by brief CVs. Ability of the bidder to fulfil Tiko’s requirements. 2. Technical approach and execution plan — 30% Proposals must contain details of the proposed approach to be adopted to deliver the service in accordance with the scope of work. 3. Financial quotation — 10% Proposals should clearly indicate whether bid participants have the financial capacity to meet the requirements of the scope of work, based on the previous value of similar work undertaken, for example by sharing copies of recent audited financial statements. 4. References — 10% Submission of at least three relevant and contactable clients previously served. 5. Capacity — 20% Proposals should clearly indicate whether bid participants have the capacity to meet the requirements of the scope of work. Total: 100%

How to Apply: **Proposal submission guidelines** Registered firms are invited to submit proposals for this engagement. Firms may apply for one or more markets and must clearly identify the countries covered by their proposals. Proposals should include the contents below and must not exceed 15 pages, excluding annexures comprising the budget and summary profiles of proposed personnel: 1. **Cover page:** Summary with basic information such as the firm’s name, address, contact information, proposed budget and countries applied for. 2. **Capacity statement:** A brief capacity statement explaining why your firm and proposed team are well positioned to undertake the engagement. 3. **Qualifications to the scope of work:** Any qualifications or reservations that you may have regarding the scope of work. 4. **Proposed approach:** Your proposed approach to delivering the scope of work requirements. 5. **Proposed personnel:** The qualifications and experience of the proposed personnel. 6. **Work plan:** Proposed work plan with tasks, responsible persons and timeline. 7. **Financial proposal:** Hourly rates in USD for each proposed role/position identified in the proposal. 8. **References:** At least three relevant and contactable references for similar engagements undertaken by the firm in the last five years. The submission must be clear, concise, and complete. Applicants should submit only such information as is necessary to respond effectively to this request for proposals. Unless specifically requested, extraneous presentation materials are neither necessary nor desired. **Expression of interest and clarification questions** Interested firms are requested to express their interest and/or submit clarification questions by emailing **bidding@tiko.org** on or before **Thursday, 22 October 2026 at 12h00 South African Standard Time (SAST, UTC+2)**. Use the subject line: **Sub-Grantee Compliance Audits: \[Firm name\]** Tiko will circulate consolidated clarification responses to all firms that have registered their interest by **Monday, 26 October 2026 at 12h00 SAST,** whether or not they submitted questions. **Submission deadline** Submit technical and financial proposals by email to [**bidding@tiko.org**](https://reliefweb.int/bidding@tiko.org) no later than **Friday, 30 October 2026 at 12h00 midday South African Standard Time (SAST, UTC+2 / 10h00 UTC)**. Use the subject line: **RFP – Sub-Grantee Compliance Audits – \[Country/Countries\]: \[Firm name\]**

title: East Africa Programme Officer
description:
Job Title: East Africa Programme Officer Reports To: Africa Regional Manager Status: Full-Time Direct Reports: Interns/volunteers, where relevant. (At present, this role doesn’t have direct reports) Contract duration: Two years (with the possibility of extension depending on funding) Compensation: ETB 2,093,000–2,898,000 annually Location: This post is based in Addis Abba, Ethiopia. Please note that IDC is unable to support relocation and the postholder needs to have the ability to work in Ethiopia. Background International Detention Coalition (IDC) is a unique global network, of over 200 civil society organisations and individuals in more than 75 countries, that coordinates with members and partners on advocacy, research, coalition and capacity building, to eliminate immigration detention and advance rights-based alternatives to detention. Role Purpose We are seeking a highly organized and motivated individual with a solid background in advocacy on migration and human rights. The ideal candidate will coordinate projects, initiatives and events efficiently, contribute to strategic advocacy efforts and support the development of the capacity of IDC members. Strong communications, organizational, planning, and stakeholder engagement skills are essential. Role Summary The Africa Programme Officer will play a key role in supporting IDC’s mission in the region by combining strong organizational and coordination skills with a solid understanding of advocacy on migration and human rights. Working closely with the Africa Regional Manager and other team members, the Programme Officer will contribute to the design and implementation of regional programs, events, initiatives and advocacy strategies. The role involves providing operational, administrative, research, and communications support, as well as helping to strengthen networks with members, partners, decision makers and other key stakeholders across the Africa region and specifically in Eastern Africa. The Programme Officer should be available to travel within the region as needed. Role Responsibilities Project implementation, admin support and support to IDC members and partners Contribute to the implementation of national and regional projects and events by providing technical, administrative, and logistical support to the Africa Regional Programme and in collaboration with relevant IDC staff and members Support the overall implementation of IDC’s mission and strategic priorities in the Africa region (with a priority focus on Easter Africa) through a balance of operational efficiency and advocacy engagement. Support IDC’s members in the region and support in network building. Maintain a high level of organization in managing project timelines, deliverables, and follow-ups in coordination with the Africa Regional Manager and other relevant team members. Support administrative processes related with finances in the Africa Programme. Advocacy and Stakeholder Engagement Support the development and implementation of advocacy strategies related to immigration detention, alternatives to detention, and broader migrant and refugee rights. Engage effectively and in coordination with the Africa Regional Manager and other relevant team members with a wide range of stakeholders, including government representatives, civil society actors, UN agencies, and regional networks, to build partnerships and advance shared objectives. Contribute to drafting and disseminating advocacy materials, briefing notes, and strategic communications tailored to diverse audiences across the Africa region. Maintain regular contact with IDC members and partners to identify policy gaps, advocacy opportunities, and spaces for support, partnership and coordinated action. Assist in the planning and facilitation of stakeholder consultations, trainings, and regional events that promote rights-based alternatives, pathways and regional dialogue. Communication Assist with developing print and digital communication materials for the region, including social media material for different platforms. Disseminate and share resources among members and other stakeholders through different platforms. Contribute to monitoring media platforms and keep track of reports and updates on relevant developments in the region. Internal Systems, Monitoring, Fundraising, and Institutional Support Actively contribute to IDC’s fundraising efforts by providing background research, identifying potential funders, coordinating inputs, and play an active role in the drafting of proposals aligned with regional priorities Ensure accurate and timely monitoring and reporting of programmatic activities, supporting internal evaluation processes and donor accountability in line with IDC’s MEL systems. Maintain organized records of project outcomes, stakeholder engagement, and communications to support institutional memory and knowledge sharing. Assist in the preparation of high-quality reports, updates, and documentation for internal use, funders, and external dissemination. Support budget tracking, planning, and financial monitoring processes in collaboration with the Regional Manager, Executive Director, and relevant IDC staff. Core Responsibilities Actively contribute to a culture of collaboration, teamwork, and support within the IDC team. Demonstrate a passion for and alignment with the IDC’s mission, vision and core values of innovation, collaboration, respect, representation and being solutions-focused Demonstrate an understanding of IDC policies including IDC Children and Vulnerable Adults Safeguarding policy to ensure a positive and safe working environment for all. Actively engage with organisational systems, processes, and infrastructure to ensure sustainability and appropriate safeguarding of institutional knowledge, assets and core activities over time Key Selection Criteria Essential Criteria Demonstrated understanding of the Africa contexts, particularly related to migration, human rights, and advocacy. A university degree in a relevant field such as international relations, law, migration studies, political science, or social sciences. A minimum of five years of professional experience, including project coordination, stakeholder engagement, and advocacy in the migration and/or human rights sectors. Proven experience in reporting and follow-up, including contributions to monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) processes and reporting experience. Strong communication, writing, and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and work independently in a remote setting. Experience engaging effectively with diverse stakeholders, including civil society, government actors, and international organizations, to advance advocacy and collaboration. Demonstrated ability to plan, organize, and facilitate events such as meetings, workshops, and advocacy activities. Excellent organizational and coordination including good attention to detail. The ability to take initiative and to work remotely and autonomously, to manage competing deadlines, prioritise workload appropriately and work in a flexible manner. Proficiency in using digital communication tools and platforms, including social media. Ability to undertake travel in the region for the role Residing in Ethiopia with the legal right to work. Fluency in both English and Amharic (written and spoken) is mandatory. Fluency in Somali and/or Arabic is an added advantage. Strong commitment to IDC’s mission and values, including its safeguarding and child protection principles.

How to Apply: **Application Process** To apply for this role, please upload your resume and a cover letter in English on [IDC Careers’ Webpage](https://idc.bamboohr.com/careers/48?source=aWQ9MjM%3D), by 8**th November** 2026. **Please ensure that you** **clearly address all of the key selection criteria in your application.** If you have enquiries, please write to jobs@idcoalition.org, please note that no application will be accepted if sent by email. **All applications must be submitted in English including cover letter & CV.** Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. The selected candidate will be expected to start as soon as possible. We envision a world where immigration detention no longer exists. And we work with everyone to make that vision a reality. We believe people should be able to live freely while they await the outcome of their immigration case, and we advocate for the human rights and dignity of everyone impacted by immigration detention. IDC is solutions-focused, meaning that we work with lived experience leaders, governments, decision-makers, civil society, UN agencies and other actors to deliver alternatives that benefit migrants, communities and society at large. We are truly global, uniting a coalition of civil society organisations, community groups and individuals from all over the world. While the movement spans continents, we all have a clear purpose: to reduce and ultimately end immigration detention and to promote alternatives. IDC values diversity, equality and inclusivity. Applications are welcome from all backgrounds. We especially encourage applications of those from underrepresented backgrounds, including but not limited to gender, race, age, sexual orientation, disability and religion. **In particular, we highly encourage leaders with lived experience of the impacts of detention to apply.** If potential candidates require any adaptations to usual recruitment processes, please do not hesitate to note this in your application.

title: Head of Advocacy and Evidencing
description:
Location: Ethiopia, India, Italy, Jordan, Kenya (as long as HelpAge International holds the registration in this country), Nepal, Pakistan, Spain, Tanzania, Thailand, Türkiye, United Kingdom and Zimbabwe Department: Global Impact Reports to (Line Manager): Director of Global Impact Responsible for (Line managing) Humanitarian Advocacy Advisor Social Protection Advisor Health Advisor Rights Advisor Grade: F Contract Type: Open-ended contract About HelpAge HelpAge International works with a diverse global network of around 200 organisations across 99 countries to promote the rights of older people to lead dignified, healthy and secure lives. Through partnership and collaborations, we work to ensure the inclusion of older people across society and strive to deliver a just and fair world for everyone as they get older. Our work is driven by our desire to achieve real impact for older people, to be inclusive, to work in partnership and to learn from our shared experience. About the Job The Head of Advocacy & Evidencing provides strategic leadership and organisational accountability for HelpAge’s global advocacy, policy and research agendas, ensuring that external engagement is grounded in rigorous evidence, shaped by the lived experiences of older people, and aligned with organisational priorities. Key areas for impact/influence and responsibilities To deliver impact, the Head of Advocacy & Evidencing will: Lead the delivery and evolution of HelpAge’s global advocacy and research agenda, ensuring it reflects lived experience and drives progress on rights, inclusion, and equity for older people. Strengthen the capacities of network members and older people to lead and participate meaningfully in advocacy efforts, and ensure inclusive engagement in the design and implementation of influencing strategies. Cultivate strategic partnerships with policy, academic, and research institutions to co-produce high-quality, policy-relevant evidence and promote HelpAge’s thought leadership on rights, healthy ageing, humanitarian inclusion, and social protection. Key Responsibilities Strategic Leadership and Advocacy Lead and be accountable for the development, implementation and results of HelpAge’s global advocacy and evidencing strategy, aligned with HelpAge’s impact areas and co-created with network members. Monitor and respond to global, regional and national policy trends,advising colleagues and network members on opportunities for engagement and influence. Champion inclusive, partner-led advocacy approaches that centre the voices and leadership of older people and civil society actors. Collaborate with the Fundraising and Strategic Partnerships Director and supporting members to align donor advocacy efforts with organisational priorities and global influencing strategies. Advise the Executive Leadership Group and the Board on HelpAge's advocacy positions and external positioning, and lead the preparation and quality of the related papers and briefings. Where appropriate, represent HelpAge's positions externally alongside senior leaders. Lead and coordinate HelpAge's influencing in priority global and regional policy and donor markets, including Europe, identifying opportunities to position ageing and the rights of older people within relevant policy, development and humanitarian agendas and, in collaboration with Fundraising, strengthen HelpAge's positioning with institutional donors and partners. Be accountable for achieving the agreed Advocacy & Evidencing income target. Working in partnership with the Fundraising & Strategic Partnerships team, play a lead technical and relationship role in shaping fundable propositions, contributing to pipeline development, and donor cultivation and stewardship for advocacy and research. Ensure that advocacy, research and evidence-generation activities comply with HelpAge’s ethical, safeguarding, data protection and relevant organisational standards, and hold team members accountable for compliance within their areas of responsibility. Represent HelpAge at senior level in key global and regional coalitions, alliances and policy forums, proactively building strategic relationships with governments, multilateral and donor institutions, policy actors and other influential stakeholders to advance HelpAge’s advocacy priorities and strengthen its external positioning. Evidence and Research Lead and be accountable for HelpAge’s global research and evidence agenda, ensuring that it is coherent, ethical, inclusive and aligned with organisational advocacy and programme priorities. Provide strategic oversight of HelpAge’s global portfolio of evidence generation, policy analysis and advocacy initiatives across key impact areas, ensuring coherence, quality and alignment with organisational strategy and drawing on the network as a central source of evidence and insight. Foster partnerships with academic institutions, think tanks, and research bodies to co-produce and validate robust, policy-influencing evidence. Ensure that research outputs are accessible, actionable, and designed for strategic influence at global and national levels. Capacity Strengthening and Network Engagement Lead on advocacy capacity strengthening of HelpAge network members and older people through mentoring, training, and tailored support. Promote knowledge exchange and peer learning across the global network, ensuring inclusive participation in advocacy platforms and decision-making spaces. Collaborate with regional colleagues to support the development and implementation of national and regional advocacy strategies led by network members. Team and Resource Management Lead, manage, and coach a multidisciplinary team of advocacy advisers, ensuring high performance and alignment with organisational goals. These are hybrid roles, with approximately 50% of their time dedicated to global advocacy and the remaining 50% focused on technical support to network members and contribution to programme development. Manage advocacy and research budgets effectively, ensuring compliance with donor requirements and strategic resource allocation. Cross-Organisational Collaboration Work closely with Programme Support, Network Development, MEAL, Fundraising, and Communications teams to embed evidence and influencing in all areas of work. Coordinate joint advocacy and research initiatives that connect policy engagement with programme delivery and impact measurement. Skills and experience required Essential Proven strategic leadership in global advocacy, policy influencing, and research within the international development, humanitarian, or human rights sectors. Strong leadership, planning, and performance management skills, with a track record of delivering results through high-performing, diverse, and remote multidisciplinary teams. Deep understanding and practical application of rights-based, inclusive, and intersectional approaches—especially relating to age, gender, disability, and displacement. Demonstrated success in designing and implementing partner-led advocacy strategies that centre lived experience and community priorities. Experience influencing policy at national, regional and international levels through coalition-building and senior-level relationships with governments, multilateral bodies and donors. Strong analytical and research skills, with experience designing or overseeing ethical, participatory research and translating evidence into compelling policy and advocacy outputs. Demonstrated ability to build and sustain high-impact partnerships with academic institutions, think tanks and policy platforms. Track record of securing income for advocacy or research, including developing fundable propositions and engaging institutional donors with fundraising colleagues. Skilled in budget oversight and resource management, including accountability in donor-funded initiatives. Ability to monitor advocacy impact, policy trends, and funding landscapes, and to adapt strategies accordingly. Experience of strengthening the capacity of civil society, networks or grassroots movements, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, through mentoring, training and tailored support. Lived experience of the Global South or extensive professional experience working in Global South contexts. Desirable Strong knowledge and networks in European/global institutional policy and donor environments Experience engaging with media to support advocacy. Education and Qualifications Degree in international development, public policy, human rights, social sciences, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience). A postgraduate qualification is an asset but not essential where practical experience is strong. Other Requirements Willingness to travel internationally Ability to work across cultures, sectors, and geographies in inclusive and equitable ways. Excellent communication skills in English (spoken and written); additional languages used in the Global South (e.g., Spanish, French, Arabic) are highly desirable. Deep commitment to locally led development and the principles of Partner-Led Programming. We actively value and encourage candidates with lived experience of inequality, marginalisation, or systemic exclusion—especially related to age, gender, disability, displacement, or economic injustice. Familiarity with ageing, inclusion, and rights issues in Global South contexts is a key asset. Key Behavioural Competencies Working Collaboratively with Others: Work collaboratively, building mutual trust and respect, with external organisations and partners to achieve our strategic aims and objectives; being accountable for the work we do together. Adaptability and Flexibility: Adapt to new directions or opportunities arising within the organisation and in our work area; being flexible in our role, constantly using the feedback to learn more and evolve further. Supporting and Facilitating Change: Lead behavioural and cultural change through embracing a supportive, collaborative and highly inclusive environment where everybody feels supported, respected and engaged. Extend HelpAge’s Reach and Impact: Extend HelpAge’s reach and impact by creating and identifying new business development opportunities and building relationships with new partners. Diversity and Inclusion: Lead and promote a culture of including the voices of older people across our support, convening and thought leadership roles, in a way that is transformative, empowering and highly inclusive of those marginalised by gender, economic status, disability and other factors of discrimination. Leading Others (for managers): Demonstrate strong leadership to own unit/department and manage people in a well and reputable manner. Create an atmosphere of trust and an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential. Safeguarding HelpAge International is committed to safeguarding the communities with which we work, our partners, staff and any others who we come into contact with. The post holder will also be responsible for: Preventing harm and abuse from our people, operations and programmes to anyone that encounters our work. Reporting all safeguarding incidents you see, hear, hear about or suspect, using our internal reporting mechanism. Complying with all safeguarding framework policies and practices. Completing mandatory training courses relating to our safeguarding policy framework and complying with HR vetting procedures. description:
Desired start date: 01/12/2026 Duration of the mission: 6 Months Location: Adwa - Tigray Region SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI) is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms. PRESENTATION OF THE MISSION: Solidarités International (SI) was registered in Ethiopia in December 2022, having previously implemented a WASH in Health intervention in Jijiga, Somali Region, in 2017. In November 2023, SI became the first humanitarian actor to operate in Mao Komo Special woreda (Benishangul-Gumuz) by rehabilitating water points in areas that had been inaccessible for three years. Currently, SI is operational in two regions of the country (In Tigray Region and Amhara Region). In Tigray, bordering Eritrea, focusing on hard-to-reach areas in partnership with Mums for Mums (MfM) SI is implementing an emergency multisectoral humanitarian programme in Ahsea and Rama Woredas of central zone, to support communities affected by drought, conflict, and displacement. Running from September 2024 to December 2025 (which is now to be extended until end of June 2026), the project aims to improve access to safe water, health services, and nutrition support, while addressing gender-based violence and mental health needs. Key activities include rehabilitating water systems and health facilities, community-based malnutrition screening, cash assistance for vulnerable households, and capacity-building for local actors. In Amhara region, Solidarités International (SI) and Première Urgence Internationale (PUI) are jointly implementing an integrated emergency response program in the Amhara region of Ethiopia, primarily focused on Health and Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) services. This program is part of a wider effort to address the significant humanitarian needs in the region caused by ongoing conflict and displacement. SI has been granted cost extension (the donor contract is extended until end of June 2026 with additional fund allocation) of existing project in Tigray and is looking for a Field Coordinator to continue the project activities in the same area. GENERAL OBJECTIVES : The Field Coordinator is the representative of the organization at field level. He/she proposes a strategy for his/her area, according to the geopolitical and humanitarian context, and ensures its implementation once validated. He/she checks and ensures that projects are carried out in accordance with the Solidarités International charter, respecting all internal and contractual procedures. He/she mobilizes the material and financial resources necessary for programs to run smoothly and supervises resource management. He/she coordinates the teams in place and is responsible for their security in his/her assigned zone. Representation and Internal / external communication: The FC is the official representative of Solidarités International in his/her intervention zone for NGOs, administrative, political and local authorities and civil society. He/She participates in humanitarian forums and relevant coordination meetings The FC Ensure that documents produced in his/her intervention zone meet deadlines and quality standards, respecting standard formats and procedures The FC Organise regular Base meetings and Ensure that key operational information circulates properly, in his/her intervention zone and between the bases and the country coordination (sitrep). ISSUES AND SPECIFIC CHALLENGES : Implement activities across several woredas in a volatile and operationally constrained context, while ensuring quality, compliance and timely delivery of ongoing projects. Maintain access and programme continuity despite recurrent constraints linked to fuel availability, cash liquidity, telecommunications/network coverage, road access and market fluctuations. Maintain adequate preparedness for a potential deterioration of the security situation, including possible disruption of banking services, communications and movements. PRIORITIES ON THE 2-3 FIRST MONTHS : -Consolidate the base management structure and ensure clear responsibilities, delegation and reporting lines within Programme and Support teams. -Ensure timely implementation and close monitoring of ongoing activities through updated workplans, APU/OFU/LFU and procurement plans. -Strengthen coordination between WASH, Livelihoods, MEAL and Support departments and ensure adequate balance of management capacity between the main programme components. -Reinforce budget forecasting and absorption monitoring. -Maintain and strengthen coordination with local authorities, clusters, partners and other humanitarian actors to avoid duplication and identify operational synergies. -Ensure the base is prepared for emergency scenarios through updated contingency plans, communication systems, cash/fuel contingency measures and staff preparedness, especially this year with the evolving context -Continue effort of base development with upcoming opportunities SECURITY CONSTRAINTS : The security environment in Tigray remains potentially volatile and can evolve rapidly, requiring continuous monitoring and strict compliance with SI security procedures. Main operational constraints include possible access restrictions, interruptions to telecommunications and internet, fuel shortages, banking/cash limitations and disruptions to road movements. Some operational areas may have limited or no network coverage, requiring reinforced movement tracking and communication procedures. The Field Coordinator must maintain a high level of preparedness, regularly review contingency arrangements, ensure critical resources are available, and adapt programme implementation and movements according to changes in the security and access environment. Staff safety and duty of care must remain central to operational decision-making. YOUR PROFIL : DIPLOMAS : A master’s degree (or equivalent field experience) in Humanitarian Action, International Development, Social Sciences, Project Management, or a related field is required. EXPERIMENT IN THE HUMANITARIAN SECTOR : more than 5 years EXPERIMENT ON SIMILAR POSITIONS : 3-4 years TECHNICAL SKILLS : Relevant management skills :Operation and team management skills include leadership, communication, and problem-solving as core competencies. Other essential skills are decision-making, time management, adaptability, and organizational abilities. Including a strong understanding of finance, and logistics processes. TRANSVERSAL SKILLS : Ability to work under pressure in a challenging and sometimes insecure environment; cultural sensitivity, adaptability, and a strong commitment to humanitarian principles and safeguarding policies (PSEA, Child Protection). LANGUAGES : Fluency in written and spoken English is essential. Knowledge of the local language(s) (e.g., Amharic, Tigrigna) is a strong asset. SI WILL OFFER YOU : A salaried position: According to experience, starting from EUR 3080 gross per month (2800 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 400. SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment. Breaks: During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked. Insurance package: Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded. Living conditions: Guest House conditions : - There will be shared guesthouse both at the project and coordination during the visit. -Internet and telephone network : Available both in Addis and Adwa -Restaurant & social life: Restaurants are available in Addis and also Adwa : - Social life in Adwa is limited. All the basics food items and other are available but there is strict limitations and taxation to importation of food. Food in your luggage however is allowed and you can stock up on specials from home. Good quality chocolate, cereals and dried meat products can be hard to find and/or very expensive.

title: Ethiopia Senior Tree Expansion Research Officer (Fixed-Term)

About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. Candidates with academic backgrounds in Forestry, Agroforestry, Agriculture, Natural Resource Management, Environmental Science, Geography, Rural Development, Watershed Management, or related fields are preferred. Experience 2 years or more of relevant professional experience in forestry, agroforestry, agriculture, natural resource management, landscape restoration, rural development, field innovation, government relations, or related fields. Experience conducting research, data collection, expansion assessments, market assessments, or strategic planning. Experience working with government institutions, development partners, or community stakeholders. Experience supporting field assessments or validation exercises is an advantage. Willingness to travel to rural and remote locations for field scouting and stakeholder engagement. Skills Strong analytical, research, and problem-solving skills. Excellent data gathering, analysis, and report writing skills. Ability to synthesize complex information into practical recommendations for decision-making. Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills. Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Ability to useMicrosoft Office, particularly Excel, PowerPoint, and Word. Experience using digital data collection tools is an advantage. Languages Can communicate in English. Fluency in Amharic. title: Government Relations Advisor, Africa
description:
PLEASE NOTE: This search is being conducted by Ethiojobs. Please apply DIRECTLY through the link below : https://ethiojobs.net/job/UAVcbgg81M-government-relations-advisor-africa-vital-strategies _________________ Vital Strategies is an international public health organization. Our programs strengthen public health systems and address the world’s leading causes of illness, injury and death. We currently work in 73 countries, supporting data-driven decision making in government, advancing evidence-based public health policies, and mounting strategic communication campaigns. Vital Strategies’ priorities are driven by the greatest potential to improve and save lives. They include non-communicable disease prevention, tobacco control, road safety, obesity prevention, overdose prevention, environmental health, and vital statistics systems building. Our programs are primarily concentrated in low- and middle-income countries in Africa, Latin America, Asia and the Pacific. Please visit our website at www.vitalstrategies.org to find out more about our work. Vital Strategies is committed to building a diverse, equitable and inclusive (DEI) organization. We believe our programs are strengthened when they are developed and supported by individuals with diverse life experiences, whose understanding of social and cultural issues can help make our work and workforce more inclusive. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. Lead Poisoning Prevention Program: Vital Strategies is expanding our program that addresses the issue of lead poisoning in low- and middle-income countries. We plan to build upon existing efforts and interest by collaborating with governmental agencies in countries in Africa, Asia, and Latin America to strengthen health systems and build local expertise in childhood lead exposure to enact sound, cost-effective policies to address exposures. Job Purpose: The position of Government Relations Advisor, Africa will facilitate regional exchange and coordinate high-level engagement and partnership building for the Lead Poisoning Prevention Program across multiple countries in Africa. The role will focus on managing and strengthening relationships with key government and program partners, stakeholders, facilitating regional exchanges and strategy development, and ensuring program alignment with countries’ priorities and global objectives. The incumbent will work closely with country teams to support government engagement, partnership building, share updates on implementation progress, and ensure exchange and coordination among government and consortium partners across the regional portfolio. The role will also provide representation at regional events, support policy engagement, and ensure effective collaboration among regional stakeholders and technical partners. It is preferred that this role be based in Ethiopia, on a full-time hybrid schedule, out of Vital Strategies' office in Addis Ababa, but we are also open to qualified candidates from Ghana, Rwanda, and Tanzania. The candidate must have authorization to work legally in the respective country at the time of hire. Vital Strategies offers highly competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits. The salary range for this position will vary by location, experience and qualifications. Duties and Responsibilities: Regional program coordination and strategic vision - · In coordination with the global team, facilitate regional exchanges and development of regional partnerships and a consistent strategy for government engagement and partnership building in the region; · Initiate and/or sustain government partnerships with ministries, regulatory bodies, and other national and regional institutions in priority countries; · Support project launches and startups in new countries within the region, including support for staff recruitment; · Support country teams in translating strategy into implementation plans, including identification of key capacity gaps to be filled, and government engagement needed to ensure quality and timely delivery of program activities; · Identify and participate in regional opportunities and events that help elevate lead poisoning on national agendas; · Promote multisectoral collaboration and partnership-driven approaches to environmental health policy development; · Manage relationships with regional organizations engaged in lead-related activities, and develop, where appropriate, formal or contractual relationships for discrete programmatic activities in support of the initiative. Partnership Management - · Support country teams in managing key government and institutional partners across the region, as well as non-government organizations in relevant sectors; · Represent Vital Strategies in regional lead poisoning prevention meetings, technical forums, public hearings, and governance bodies in the region; · Support the development and review of reports, policy briefs, and training materials developed in the region; · Promote cross-sector dialogues that support the development of integrated, evidence-based public policies; · Facilitate knowledge exchange across the region; · Coordinate work with national and international partners, ensuring alignment across local and global strategies; · Assist with other duties as specified by the supervisor. Qualifications: Education & Degree - · Master’s degree in public health, public policy/Administration, Global Health, international development, environmental health science, or related field. Skills & Abilities - · Strong government engagement and partnership-building skills, with the ability to establish and sustain relationships with ministries, regulatory bodies, and regional institutions; · Demonstrated ability to coordinate multi-country initiatives and facilitate regional exchange and collaboration; · Strategic thinking skills, with the ability to translate regional strategy into actionable country-level implementation plans; · Strong stakeholder management skills across government, NGOs, multilateral agencies, and technical partners; · Ability to promote and facilitate multisectoral collaboration and policy dialogue; · Ability to monitor program quality, performance, and outcomes across a regional portfolio; · Ability to coordinate and engage program stakeholders and other country teams; · Demonstrated sensitivity in handling confidential information; · Proven ability to interpret public health data, generate actionable insights, and support policy recommendations; · Exhibits strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple competing priorities and meet deadlines; demonstrates personal integrity, credibility, and professionalism while taking initiative and making sound, informed decisions in a fast-paced environment; · Professional oral and written proficiency in English; · Excellent interpersonal skills, including the ability to communicate effectively to technical and non-technical audiences, and contribute to an interdisciplinary international team; · Solid knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook); · Experience working with a geographically distributed team with demonstrated ability to work collaboratively, communicate clearly and regularly, monitor performance, and inspire, engage, and motivate staff; · Demonstrated commitment to contributing to an inclusive working and learning environment. Experience: Required - · Minimum of eight years of experience in government engagement and public health programming, ideally with experience in health policy, environmental health, and/or global health, especially related to lead poisoning prevention or environmental pollution; · Experience in representing organizations with governments, international institutions, and senior stakeholder forums; · Experience managing multi-country programs in Africa; · Experience working with government agencies, regulatory bodies, and public health facilities; · Experience with program reporting and monitoring. Preferred - · Demonstrated experience in communicating scientific and health information to varied audiences; · Experience in using project management platforms. Working Conditions and Physical Requirements: · If hired in Ghana, Rwanda, or Tanzania, the candidate will be hired via Vital Strategies’ Employer of Record on a remote schedule; · The position will require travel up to 30% of the time to visit operating countries in the region to visit field implementation or attend meetings with partners; · The candidate needs to be willing to work with colleagues across different time zones.

description:
Support Service Team Leader 

 

The Danish Refugee Council (DRC), one of the world’s leading NGOs, with a focus on responding to displacement, have been registered in Sudan since 2004, delivering life-saving programming in protection, emergency response, shelter, food security and livelihoods, disaster risk reduction, camp management, and humanitarian mine action. DRC has implemented projects in Central Darfur, South Kordofan, Gedaref, Port Sudan, and White Nile. Sudan hosts one of the largest displaced populations in Africa, with over 3.7 million internally displaced people and over 1.1 million refugees from South Sudan, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Central African Republic, Chad, Yemen and Syria. Against a background of political crisis, Sudan faces economic and social turmoil, with sharp increases in food and energy costs, further exacerbated by disease outbreaks and ongoing conflict.

 

POSITION PROFILE

The purpose of the Support Services Team Leader is to coordinate the support functions at Area Office. Responsibilities encompass all support activities for the DRC Gedaref office. This role has an area focus and ensures compliance with DRC procedures and guidelines within the area office.
